title: The bullet and what it leaves behind
summary: A bullet in R.E.P.O. is an object with its own behaviour: it can carry a hurt collider with a timer, it plants a mark where it lands, that mark has a time before it is cleaned up, and it can trail extra particles of its own.
body: A shot is not only a number taken off a creature. What leaves the gun is an object of its own, which is why firing can leave something in the level rather than only changing a value.
It can hurt what it reaches. A bullet carries a flag for whether it has a hurt collider at all, and the collider itself when it does, so not every projectile has to be able to injure something.
That ability is timed. There is a timer attached to the hurt collider, which is why a bullet can stop being dangerous without the bullet being removed.
It puts a mark where it lands. There is a hit object that the bullet carries, which is how a shot can be seen on a wall or a floor rather than only heard.
The mark goes away on its own. There is a time before that hit object is destroyed, so a level does not fill up with the results of every shot the crew has fired.
It can also be dressed. There is an extra particles object that a bullet can be given, so the same projectile can look different depending on what fired it or what it hits.
What this entry does not tell you: how much damage a bullet does, how long the hurt collider lasts, or how long a mark stays. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: A bullet can carry a hurt collider and a flag for whether it has one.
There is a timer on that hurt collider.
It carries a hit object that it leaves where it lands.
That hit object has a time before it is destroyed.
It can carry extra particles, with a flag for whether it has them.

alt.en: Diagram: a bullet flies, can hurt what it reaches for a time, leaves a mark where it lands, and that mark is cleaned up after its own time.
alt.zh: 示意图：子弹飞出、在一段时间内可造成伤害、落地留下痕迹，痕迹在自身计时后消失。
